_comment: Bus vectors for the DS3231 real-time clock, shared by the tab model (frontend/src/simulation/I2CBusManager.ts, vitest) and the backend twin (backend/app/services/esp32_i2c_slaves.py, pytest). The format is in README.md next to this file. Register facts are from the datasheet, 19-5170 rev 10; driver traces name the source they were read from. The host's clock starts every vector at 12:34:56.250 of Wednesday 30 September 2026, and the firmware was built on 29 September 2026 at 23:39:41.

vectors.name: power-on: the host's time with Monday as day 1, CONTROL 0x1C, STATUS 0x08 with OSF clear, 25.00 C
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Control Register (0Eh) and Status Register (0Fh), POR rows. OSF is 0, not the datasheet's first power-up: the part is a module somebody set and whose battery kept it running, as the DS1307 powers on with CH 0. The host's time is the model's. Monday = 1: RTClib dowToDS3231

vectors.name: the address pointer wraps from 0x12 to 0x00, in a read and in a write
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Address Map: when the address pointer reaches the end of the register space (12h), it wraps around to location 00h

vectors.name: the pointer stays where a transfer left it, across the STOP
vectors.spec: Datasheet, I2C Serial Data Bus, data read: the register pointer keeps the last address

vectors.name: the time is latched at START and again when the pointer rolls over to 0x00
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Clock and Calendar: the user buffers are synchronized to the internal registers on any START and when the register pointer rolls over to zero

vectors.name: a time the sketch sets is kept, and the clock counts from the moment the seconds were written
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Clock and Calendar: the countdown chain is reset whenever the seconds register is written. Decision D7: a date of the sketch's own is kept

vectors.name: bit 7 of the seconds does not exist: the DS3231 has no clock halt
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Figure 1: bit 7 of register 00h is 0. Control Register: powered by VCC the oscillator is always on

vectors.name: the century bit is kept as written and turns over when the year goes from 99 to 00
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Clock and Calendar: the century bit (bit 7 of the month register) is toggled when the years register overflows from 99 to 00

vectors.name: 12-hour mode: the hours count in the form they were written in
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Clock and Calendar: bit 6 of the hours register selects the 12-hour mode; in it bit 5 is the AM/PM bit, high being PM

vectors.name: CONTROL keeps what is written but CONV, which is over by the next read, and BSY reads 0
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Control Register: CONV. The conversion takes no time in the model (decision D5). Makuna Rtc RtcDS3231::ForceTemperatureCompensationUpdate polls CONV until it reads 0

vectors.name: OSF is clear at power-on and a write of 1 does not set it; EN32kHz reads back
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Status Register: OSF can only be written to logic 0; the chip sets it when its oscillator stops, which this model's never does. Bits 6 to 4 read 0. RTClib RTC_DS3231::lostPower is register 0x0F >> 7, enable32K and disable32K write bit 3

vectors.name: the alarm registers keep what is written
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Figure 1: alarm 1 at 07h to 0Ah, alarm 2 at 0Bh to 0Dh. RTClib getAlarm1, getAlarm2, getAlarm1Mode

vectors.name: alarm 1 on hours, minutes and seconds: A1F is set at the second that matches, stays, and is cleared by writing it to 0
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Alarms and Table 2; Status Register: A1F is cleared when written to logic 0. RTClib 2.1.4 setAlarm1(12:35:00 of the 30th, DS3231_A1_Hour), alarmFired(1), clearAlarm(1)

vectors.name: the flags are set whether or not the interrupt is enabled, and writing a flag to 1 leaves it as it is
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Control Register: the corresponding alarm flag is always set regardless of the state of the INTCN bit. Status Register: attempting to write to logic 1 leaves the value unchanged

vectors.name: alarm 1 once per second, when the seconds match, and when minutes and seconds match
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Table 2, alarm 1 mask bits 1111, 1110 and 1100

vectors.name: a second that matched while nobody read the chip has set the flag
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Alarms: the match is tested on the once-per-second update of the time and date registers

vectors.name: alarm 2 matches at second 00: once per minute, on the minute, and on hours and minutes
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Table 2, alarm 2 mask bits 111, 110 and 100. RTClib setAlarm2

vectors.name: an alarm on the date matches that day of the month and no other
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Table 2: DY/DT 0, mask bits 0000, alarm when date, hours, minutes and seconds match

vectors.name: an alarm on the day of week compares the number the clock counts, which is the one the sketch wrote
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Table 2: DY/DT 1, alarm when day, hours, minutes and seconds match. RTClib setAlarm1(..., DS3231_A1_Day) writes dowToDS3231(dayOfTheWeek()) with bit 6 set

vectors.name: an alarm in 12-hour form matches a clock in 12-hour mode, and not one in 24-hour mode
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Figure 1: the alarm hours registers have the 12/24 and AM/PM bits of the hours register, and the alarm is a match of the registers

vectors.name: setting the time does not count through the seconds in between: no alarm is owed for them
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Alarms: the match is tested on the once-per-second update. A write is not an update

vectors.name: the temperature is two's complement in quarter degrees, from the panel
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Temperature Registers (11h-12h): a 10-bit code with a resolution of 0.25 C in two's complement; the upper 8 bits at 11h, the lower 2 bits in the top of 12h. 00011001 01b = +25.25 C

vectors.name: the temperature registers are read-only, and a slider that moves in the middle of a read does not split it
vectors.spec: Datasheet, Temperature Registers: the temperature registers are read-only. The two bytes are one conversion. A host that copies the registers meanwhile gets the new one and leaves the read as it was

vectors.name: the build time of the firmware, written in one burst, leaves the clock on the host's time
vectors.spec: Decision D7. RTClib 2.1.4 RTC_DS3231::adjust(DateTime(F(__DATE__), F(__TIME__))): pointer 0, seconds, minutes, hours, day of week with Monday as 1, date, month, year; then STATUS is read and written back with OSF cleared. 29 September 2026 is a Tuesday

vectors.name: the jump from the build time to the host's time sets no alarm
vectors.spec: Decision D7: the clock was set when the firmware was built and has run since; the alarms are for what it counts from now on

vectors.name: one second away from the build time is a date of the sketch's own, and is kept
vectors.spec: Decision D7: the match is on the written date and time, to the second

vectors.name: with no build time known, the time the firmware wrote at build time is kept like any other
vectors.spec: Decision D7: if no compile time can be established for a build, a written time is kept, which is what the chip does

vectors.name: RTClib RTC_DS3231: adjust() to a date of the sketch's own, now(), getTemperature(), and an alarm 2 on the minute
vectors.spec: RTClib 2.1.4 RTC_DS3231.cpp with Adafruit BusIO 1.17.4. adjust(DateTime(2024, 2, 29, 23, 59, 30)), a Thursday: day of week 4. setAlarm2(DS3231_A2_Minute) at minute 00 after writeSqwPinMode left INTCN set; disableAlarm and clearAlarm before, as the library's example does
